question.:question/problem: Find a vector equation of the normal line to the level surface $\left(-\left(x - 2\right)\right)^{2}+2\left(-y\right)^{2}-\left(-z\right)=0$ at the point $(1,-1,-3).$
question.:question/worked-solution:
Let's set $f(x,y,z)=\left(-\left(x - 2\right)\right)^{2}+2\left(-y\right)^{2}-\left(-z\right).$ Then, our surface can be viewed as the level surface $f(x,y,z)=0.$

A normal vector to the level surface that passes through the point $(1,-1,-3)$ can be found by computing $∇f(1,-1,-3).$

So, we find the gradient and evaluate it at $(1,-1,-3):$

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f(x,y,z)&={f}_{x}(x,y,z)i+{f}_{y}(x,y,z)j+{f}_{z}(x,y,z)k\\&=\frac{∂}{∂x}(\left(-\left(x - 2\right)\right)^{2}+2\left(-y\right)^{2}-\left(-z\right))i+\frac{∂}{∂y}(\left(-\left(x - 2\right)\right)^{2}+2\left(-y\right)^{2}-\left(-z\right))j+\frac{∂}{∂z}(\left(-\left(x - 2\right)\right)^{2}+2\left(-y\right)^{2}-\left(-z\right))k\\&=\left(2 x - 4\right)i+\left(4 y\right)j+\left(1\right)k\\∇f(1,-1,-3)&=\left(-2\right)i+\left(-4\right)j+\left(1\right)k\\&=⟨-2,-4,1⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, the vector equation of the line that is parallel to $∇f(1,-1,-3)$ and passes through the point $(1,-1,-3)$ can be written as

$$r=⟨1,-1,-3⟩+t\,∇f(1,-1,-3)=⟨1,-1,-3⟩+t\,⟨-2,-4,1⟩.$$

where $t\in (-\infty,\infty).$

question.:question/problem: Find a vector equation of the normal line to the level surface $\left(-\left(x - 1\right)\right)^{2}+2\left(-\left(y - 1\right)\right)^{2}-\left(z - 2\right)=0$ at the point $(0,0,5).$
question.:question/worked-solution:
Let's set $f(x,y,z)=\left(-\left(x - 1\right)\right)^{2}+2\left(-\left(y - 1\right)\right)^{2}-\left(z - 2\right).$ Then, our surface can be viewed as the level surface $f(x,y,z)=0.$

A normal vector to the level surface that passes through the point $(0,0,5)$ can be found by computing $∇f(0,0,5).$

So, we find the gradient and evaluate it at $(0,0,5):$

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f(x,y,z)&={f}_{x}(x,y,z)i+{f}_{y}(x,y,z)j+{f}_{z}(x,y,z)k\\&=\frac{∂}{∂x}(\left(-\left(x - 1\right)\right)^{2}+2\left(-\left(y - 1\right)\right)^{2}-\left(z - 2\right))i+\frac{∂}{∂y}(\left(-\left(x - 1\right)\right)^{2}+2\left(-\left(y - 1\right)\right)^{2}-\left(z - 2\right))j+\frac{∂}{∂z}(\left(-\left(x - 1\right)\right)^{2}+2\left(-\left(y - 1\right)\right)^{2}-\left(z - 2\right))k\\&=\left(2 x - 2\right)i+\left(4 y - 4\right)j+\left(-1\right)k\\∇f(0,0,5)&=\left(-2\right)i+\left(-4\right)j+\left(-1\right)k\\&=⟨-2,-4,-1⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, the vector equation of the line that is parallel to $∇f(0,0,5)$ and passes through the point $(0,0,5)$ can be written as

$$r=⟨0,0,5⟩+t\,∇f(0,0,5)=⟨0,0,5⟩+t\,⟨-2,-4,-1⟩.$$

where $t\in (-\infty,\infty).$

question.:question/problem: Find a vector equation of the normal line to the surface $4{\left(-\left(z + 1\right)\right)}^{2}-4{\left(-\left(y + 1\right)\right)}^{2}={\left(-\left(x - 1\right)\right)}^{2}-6\left(-\left(x - 1\right)\right)+12$ at the point $(-1,-1,-2).$
question.:question/worked-solution:
First, we bring all variables to one side:

$$
\begin{aligned}4{\left(-\left(z + 1\right)\right)}^{2}-4{\left(-\left(y + 1\right)\right)}^{2} & ={\left(-\left(x - 1\right)\right)}^{2}-6\left(-\left(x - 1\right)\right) +12\\ 4{\left(-\left(z + 1\right)\right)}^{2}-4{\left(-\left(y + 1\right)\right)}^{2}-{\left(-\left(x - 1\right)\right)}^{2}+6\left(-\left(x - 1\right)\right) & =12\end{aligned}
$$

If we set $f(x,y,z)=4{\left(-\left(z + 1\right)\right)}^{2}-4{\left(-\left(y + 1\right)\right)}^{2}-{\left(-\left(x - 1\right)\right)}^{2}+6\left(-\left(x - 1\right)\right)$, our surface can be viewed as the level surface $f(x,y,z)=12.$ 

A normal vector to the level surface that passes through the point $(-1,-1,-2)$ can be found by computing $∇f(-1,-1,-2).$ 

So, we find the gradient and evaluate it at $(-1,-1,-2):$

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f(x,y,z) & ={f}_{x}(x,y,z)\,i+{f}_{y}(x,y,z)\text{ }j+{f}_{z}(x,y,z)\text{ }k \\  & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(4{\left(-\left(z + 1\right)\right)}^{2}-4{\left(-\left(y + 1\right)\right)}^{2}-{\left(-\left(x - 1\right)\right)}^{2}+6\left(-\left(x - 1\right)\right))i+\frac{∂}{∂y}(4{\left(-\left(z + 1\right)\right)}^{2}-4{\left(-\left(y + 1\right)\right)}^{2}-{\left(-\left(x - 1\right)\right)}^{2}+6\left(-\left(x - 1\right)\right))j+\frac{∂}{∂z}(4{\left(-\left(z + 1\right)\right)}^{2}-4{\left(-\left(y + 1\right)\right)}^{2}-{\left(-\left(x - 1\right)\right)}^{2}+6\left(-\left(x - 1\right)\right))k \\  & =\left(-\left((6-2\left(-\left(x - 1\right)\right))\right)\right)i+\left(-\left(-8\left(-\left(y + 1\right)\right)\right)\right)j+\left(-\left(+8\left(-\left(z + 1\right)\right)\right)\right)k\\∇f(-1,-1,-2)& =\left(-\left((6-2\left(-\left(\left(-1\right) - 1\right)\right))\right)\right)i+\left(-\left(-8\left(-\left(\left(-1\right) + 1\right)\right)\right)\right)j+\left(-\left(+8\left(-\left(\left(-2\right) + 1\right)\right)\right)\right)k\\  & =\left(-\left((6-2(2))\right)\right)i+\left(-\left(-8(0)\right)\right)j+\left(-\left(+8(1)\right)\right)k\\  & =\left(-\left(2\right)\right)i+\left(-\left(0\right)\right)j+\left(-\left(+8\right)\right)k\\  & =⟨-2,0,-8⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, the vector equation of the line that is parallel to $∇f(-1,-1,-2)$ and passes through the point $(-1,-1,-2)$ can be written as

$$
\begin{aligned}r & =⟨-1,-1,-2⟩+t\,∇f(-1,-1,-2)=⟨-1,-1,-2⟩+t\,⟨-2,0,-8⟩,\end{aligned}
$$

where $t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).$

question.:question/problem: Find a vector equation of the normal line to the surface $z=2{\left(-\left(x + 3\right)\right)}^{2}+2{\left(-y\right)}^{2}+\left(-\left(x + 3\right)\right)$ at the point $(- \frac{7}{2},-1,3).$
question.:question/worked-solution:
First, we bring all variables to one side:

$$
\begin{aligned}z & =2{\left(-\left(x + 3\right)\right)}^{2}+2{\left(-y\right)}^{2}+\left(-\left(x + 3\right)\right) \\ z-2{\left(-\left(x + 3\right)\right)}^{2}-2{\left(-y\right)}^{2}-\left(-\left(x + 3\right)\right) & =0\end{aligned}
$$

If we set $f(x,y,z)=z-2{\left(-\left(x + 3\right)\right)}^{2}-2{\left(-y\right)}^{2}-\left(-\left(x + 3\right)\right)$, our surface can be viewed as the level surface $f(x,y,z)=0.$ 

A normal vector to the level surface that passes through the point $(- \frac{7}{2},-1,3)$ can be found by computing $∇f(- \frac{7}{2},-1,3).$ 

So, we find the gradient and evaluate it at $(- \frac{7}{2},-1,3):$

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f(x,y,z) & ={f}_{x}(x,y,z)\,i+{f}_{y}(x,y,z)\text{ }j+{f}_{z}(x,y,z)\text{ }k \\  & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(z-2{\left(-\left(x + 3\right)\right)}^{2}-2{\left(-y\right)}^{2}-\left(-\left(x + 3\right)\right))i+\frac{∂}{∂y}(z-2{\left(-\left(x + 3\right)\right)}^{2}-2{\left(-y\right)}^{2}-\left(-\left(x + 3\right)\right))j+\frac{∂}{∂z}(z-2{\left(-\left(x + 3\right)\right)}^{2}-2{\left(-y\right)}^{2}-\left(-\left(x + 3\right)\right))k \\  & =\left(-\left((-4\left(-\left(x + 3\right)\right)-1)\right)\right)i+\left(-\left(-4\left(-y\right)\right)\right)j+\left(1\right)k\\∇f(- \frac{7}{2},-1,3)& =\left(-\left((-4\left(-\left(\left(- \frac{7}{2}\right) + 3\right)\right)-1)\right)\right)i+\left(-\left(-4\left(-\left(-1\right)\right)\right)\right)j+\left(1\right)k\\  & =\left(-\left((-4(\frac{1}{2})-1)\right)\right)i+\left(-\left(-4(1)\right)\right)j+\left(1\right)k\\  & =\left(-\left(-3\right)\right)i+\left(-\left(-4\right)\right)j+\left(1\right)k\\  & =⟨3,4,1⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, the vector equation of the line that is parallel to $∇f(- \frac{7}{2},-1,3)$ and passes through the point $(- \frac{7}{2},-1,3)$ can be written as

$$
\begin{aligned}r & =⟨- \frac{7}{2},-1,3⟩+t\,∇f(- \frac{7}{2},-1,3)=⟨- \frac{7}{2},-1,3⟩+t\,⟨3,4,1⟩,\end{aligned}
$$

where $t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).$

question.:question/problem: Find the equation of the normal line to the surface $\sqrt{2{\left(-\left(x - 1\right)\right)}^{2}+\left(-\left(y + 1\right)\right)-4\left(-\left(z + 1\right)\right)}=1$ at the point $(-1,-2,-3).$
question.:question/worked-solution:
Let's set $f(x,y,z)=\sqrt{2{\left(-\left(x - 1\right)\right)}^{2}+\left(-\left(y + 1\right)\right)-4\left(-\left(z + 1\right)\right)}.$ Then, our surface can be viewed as the level surface $f(x,y,z)=1.$     

A normal vector to the level surface that passes through the point $(-1,-2,-3)$ can be found by computing $∇f(-1,-2,-3).$

So, we find the gradient and evaluate it at $(-1,-2,-3):$    

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f(x,y,z) & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(\sqrt{2{\left(-\left(x - 1\right)\right)}^{2}+\left(-\left(y + 1\right)\right)-4\left(-\left(z + 1\right)\right)})\text{ }i+\frac{∂}{∂y}(\sqrt{2{\left(-\left(x - 1\right)\right)}^{2}+\left(-\left(y + 1\right)\right)-4\left(-\left(z + 1\right)\right)})\text{ }j+\frac{∂}{∂z}(\sqrt{2{\left(-\left(x - 1\right)\right)}^{2}+\left(-\left(y + 1\right)\right)-4\left(-\left(z + 1\right)\right)})\text{ }k \\  & =\left(-\left(\frac{2\left(-\left(x - 1\right)\right)}{\sqrt{2{\left(-\left(x - 1\right)\right)}^{2}+\left(-\left(y + 1\right)\right)-4\left(-\left(z + 1\right)\right)}}\right)\right)i+\left(-\left(+\frac{1}{2\sqrt{2{\left(-\left(x - 1\right)\right)}^{2}+\left(-\left(y + 1\right)\right)-4\left(-\left(z + 1\right)\right)}}\right)\right)j+\left(-\left(-\frac{2}{\sqrt{2{\left(-\left(x - 1\right)\right)}^{2}+\left(-\left(y + 1\right)\right)-4\left(-\left(z + 1\right)\right)}}\right)\right)k\\∇f(-1,-2,-3)& =\left(-\left(\frac{2\left(-\left(\left(-1\right) - 1\right)\right)}{\sqrt{2{\left(-\left(\left(-1\right) - 1\right)\right)}^{2}+\left(-\left(\left(-2\right) + 1\right)\right)-4\left(-\left(\left(-3\right) + 1\right)\right)}}\right)\right)i+\left(-\left(+\frac{1}{2\sqrt{2{\left(-\left(\left(-1\right) - 1\right)\right)}^{2}+\left(-\left(\left(-2\right) + 1\right)\right)-4\left(-\left(\left(-3\right) + 1\right)\right)}}\right)\right)j+\left(-\left(-\frac{2}{\sqrt{2{\left(-\left(\left(-1\right) - 1\right)\right)}^{2}+\left(-\left(\left(-2\right) + 1\right)\right)-4\left(-\left(\left(-3\right) + 1\right)\right)}}\right)\right)k\\  & =\left(-\left(\frac{2\cdot 2}{\sqrt{2\cdot {2}^{2}+1-4\cdot 2}}\right)\right)i+\left(-\left(+\frac{1}{2\sqrt{2\cdot {2}^{2}+1-4\cdot 2}}\right)\right)j+\left(-\left(-\frac{2}{\sqrt{2\cdot {2}^{2}+1-4\cdot 2}}\right)\right)k\\  & =\left(-\left(4\right)\right)i+\left(-\left(+\frac{1}{2}\right)\right)j+\left(-\left(-2\right)\right)k\\  & =⟨-4,- \frac{1}{2},2⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, by using the symmetric form of the equation of the line that is parallel to the vector $v=⟨{v}_{x},{v}_{y},{v}_{z}⟩$ and passes through the point $({x}_{0},{y}_{0},{z}_{0})$,  we get:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{x-{x}_{0}}{{v}_{x}}=\frac{y-{y}_{0}}{{v}_{y}}=\frac{z-{z}_{0}}{{v}_{z}} \\ \frac{\left(-\left(x - 1\right)\right)-2}{4}=\frac{\left(-\left(y + 1\right)\right)-1}{\frac{1}{2}}=\frac{\left(-\left(z + 1\right)\right)-2}{-2} \\ \frac{\left(-\left(x - 1\right)\right)-2}{4}=2\left(-\left(y + 1\right)\right)-2=\frac{2-\left(-\left(z + 1\right)\right)}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem: Find the equation of the normal line to the surface $\left(z - 1\right)=\operatorname{sin}⁡(\left(-x\right)\left(-y\right))+{\left(-y\right)}^{2}$ at the point $(0,1,2).$
question.:question/worked-solution:
First, we bring all variables to one side:

$$
\begin{aligned}\left(z - 1\right) & =\operatorname{sin}⁡(\left(-x\right)\left(-y\right))+{\left(-y\right)}^{2} \\ 0 & =\operatorname{sin}⁡(\left(-x\right)\left(-y\right))+{\left(-y\right)}^{2}-\left(z - 1\right)\end{aligned}
$$

If we set $f(x,y,z)=\operatorname{sin}⁡(\left(-x\right)\left(-y\right))+{\left(-y\right)}^{2}-\left(z - 1\right)$, our surface can be viewed as the level surface $f(x,y,z)=0.$ 

A normal vector to the level surface that passes through the point $(0,1,2)$ can be found by computing $∇f(0,1,2).$ 

So, we find the gradient and evaluate it at $(0,1,2):$

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f(x,y,z) & ={f}_{x}(x,y,z)\,i+{f}_{y}(x,y,z)\text{ }j+{f}_{z}(x,y,z)\text{ }k \\  & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(\operatorname{sin}⁡(\left(-x\right)\left(-y\right))+{\left(-y\right)}^{2}-\left(z - 1\right))i+\frac{∂}{∂y}(\operatorname{sin}⁡(\left(-x\right)\left(-y\right))+{\left(-y\right)}^{2}-\left(z - 1\right))j+\frac{∂}{∂z}(\operatorname{sin}⁡(\left(-x\right)\left(-y\right))+{\left(-y\right)}^{2}-\left(z - 1\right))k \\  & =\left(-\left(\left(-y\right)\operatorname{cos}⁡(\left(-x\right)\left(-y\right))\right)\right)i+\left(-\left(+(\left(-x\right)\operatorname{cos}⁡(\left(-x\right)\left(-y\right))+2\left(-y\right))\right)\right)j+\left(-1\right)k\\∇f(0,1,2)& =\left(-\left(\left(-\left(1\right)\right)\operatorname{cos}⁡(\left(-\left(0\right)\right)\left(-\left(1\right)\right))\right)\right)i+\left(-\left(+(\left(-\left(0\right)\right)\operatorname{cos}⁡(\left(-\left(0\right)\right)\left(-\left(1\right)\right))+2\left(-\left(1\right)\right))\right)\right)j+\left(-1\right)k\\  & =\left(-\left((-1)\operatorname{cos}⁡(0)\right)\right)i+\left(-\left(+[(0)\operatorname{cos}⁡(0)+2(-1)]\right)\right)j+\left(-1\right)k\\  & =\left(-\left(-1\right)\right)i+\left(-\left(-2\right)\right)j+\left(-1\right)k\\  & =⟨1,2,-1⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, the Cartesian equation of the line that is parallel to $v=⟨{v}_{x},{v}_{y},{v}_{z}⟩$ and passes through the point $({x}_{0},{y}_{0},{z}_{0})$ can be written as:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{x-{x}_{0}}{{v}_{x}}=\frac{y-{y}_{0}}{{v}_{y}}=\frac{z-{z}_{0}}{{v}_{z}} \\ \frac{\left(-x\right)-0}{-1}=\frac{\left(-y\right)-(-1)}{-2}=\frac{\left(z - 1\right)-1}{-1} \\ \frac{\left(-x\right)}{-1}=\frac{\left(-y\right)+1}{-2}=\frac{\left(z - 1\right)-1}{-1} \\ \frac{\left(-x\right)}{1}=\frac{\left(-y\right)+1}{2}=\frac{\left(z - 1\right)-1}{1} \\ \left(-x\right)=\frac{\left(-y\right)+1}{2}=\left(z - 1\right)-1\end{aligned}
$$
